record.nameMeaning: "Perforated lizard", for the openings in its frill
record.oneLiner: A ceratopsian bearing one of the largest skulls of any land animal.
record.description: Torosaurus was a chasmosaurine ceratopsian of the very end of the Cretaceous, 7.5–9 m long, possessing an enormous elongated frill with large openings — giving it one of the largest skulls of any known land animal (up to 2.77 m). Some researchers argue it is simply a fully mature Triceratops.

notableFacts.text: Its frilled skull (up to 2.77 m) is among the largest of any land animal.
Debated to be the mature adult form of Triceratops.
